models_evaluated: Recalibrated Framingham Risk Score model 1 (all ages)

links.outcome: Association of original vs locally recalibrated Framingham risk categories with carotid IMT
links.effect: Recalibrated models gave lower overall CHD risk estimates than the original score and showed stronger CIMT associations; CIMT differed by risk category (P<.05), with higher CIMT values in rFRS models.
links.quote: The recalibrated FRS models provided lower overall CHD risk estimates while maintaining stronger associations with CIMT than the original FRS, supporting their improved applicability for CHD risk prediction in the Sri Lankan population.

models_evaluated: Recalibrated Framingham Risk Score model 1 (rFRS model 1)
Recalibrated Framingham Risk Score model 2 (rFRS model 2)

links.outcome: CIMT association and CHD risk categorization
links.effect: rFRS lower CHD risk and stronger CIMT associations; CIMT differed by risk category for oFRS and rFRS (P<.05); composite carotid scores correlated with all FRS models (P=.001).
links.quote: The recalibrated FRS models provided lower overall CHD risk estimates while maintaining stronger associations with CIMT than the original FRS, supporting their improved applicability for CHD risk prediction in the Sri Lankan population.

links.outcome: CHD risk classification and association with carotid artery intima-media thickness
links.effect: Recalibrated FRS gave lower overall CHD risk estimates than original FRS, with 30.5% male and 68.0% female classification consistency, while showing higher CIMT values across risk categories (P<.05) and positive composite correlations (P=.001).
links.quote: The recalibrated FRS models provided lower overall CHD risk estimates while maintaining stronger associations with CIMT than the original FRS, supporting their improved applicability for CHD risk prediction in the Sri Lankan population.
